chunks: The Book of Uyun al-Akhbar and Amali of al-Saduq: Ibn al-Mutawakkil, from Ali, from his father, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, from Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, from his forefathers, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Majestic is His Majesty, said: He has not believed in Me the one who interprets My words based on his opinion, he has not known Me the one who compares Me to My creation, and he is not upon My religion the one who uses analogical reasoning in it.

key_terms.الْقِيَاسُ: Analogical reasoning (qiyas), a method of legal deduction
key_terms.تَشْبِيهٌ: Comparison or anthropomorphism (likening God to creation)
key_terms.تَفْسِيرٌ بِرَأْيٍ: Interpretation based on personal opinion or subjective reasoning

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about interpreting the Quran by personal opinion and using qiyas in religion?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi, transmitted through the Ahl al-Bayt chain, underscores the Shia emphasis on divine transcendence (tanzih) by linking subjective interpretation (tafsir bi'l-ra'y) and anthropomorphism (tashbih) as errors of human limitation. It specifically warns against applying analogical reasoning (qiyas) to religious matters, asserting that divine truth transcends human deductive methods. This serves as a foundational critique of rationalist schools that prioritize human logic over revealed text in theological derivation.
